title: U.S. House · New Mexico's 2nd District
area: Southern New Mexico, including Las Cruces and the state's border region with Mexico.

context.text: Ballotpedia identifies this as a battleground race. Incumbent Rep. Gabriel Vasquez (D) defeated then-incumbent Yvette Herrell (R) 50.3%-49.6% in 2022 and 52.1%-47.9% in 2024; in the 2024 presidential race, Donald Trump carried the district 49.9%-48.1%, making it one of 23 U.S. House districts Democrats are defending that Trump won in 2024. As of July 2026, major election forecasters rated the general election Lean Democratic or Tilt Democratic. As of June 30, 2026, Vasquez had raised $3.78 million in the cycle and Republican nominee Greg Cunningham had raised $1.51 million.

candidates.name: Gabriel Vasquez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed after fellow Democrat Tom Wakely did not make the ballot.

summary.text: Gabe Vasquez is the Democratic incumbent for New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in November 2022 when he defeated Republican incumbent Yvette Herrell. A Las Cruces native, he worked as a journalist, chamber of commerce executive and staffer for Sen. Martin Heinrich before serving on the Las Cruces City Council. He describes his focus as lowering the cost of living, expanding health care access, protecting public lands, and immigration reform.

background.text: Born in Las Cruces, New Mexico, where he lives. His official biography describes him as a first-generation Mexican-American who grew up in the borderlands and was the first in his family born in the United States.
Earned a bachelor's degree in English and journalism from New Mexico State University in 2008.

Worked as a journalist and in public relations, and as executive director of the Las Cruces Hispano Chamber of Commerce; his official biography also cites work in public lands conservation and as a policy advocate on child welfare at the federal level.
In 2013, after helping build a Las Cruces startup company, joined Sen. Martin Heinrich's staff as a field representative working across southern New Mexico, according to his official biography.
Elected to the Las Cruces City Council in 2017, representing District 3; his official biography says he won with more than 70 percent of the vote.
Won the 2nd Congressional District seat in November 2022, defeating incumbent Yvette Herrell 50.3% to 49.6%, and took office in January 2023.
Defeated Herrell again in 2024, 52.1% to 47.9%, in a district that Donald Trump won with 49.9% of the vote.
In the 119th Congress, serves on the Committee on Agriculture (Conservation Research and Biotechnology) and the Committee on Armed Services (Readiness; Strategic Forces).
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary for the seat.

priorities.text: Says he works with Democrats, Republicans and independents on issues New Mexicans care most about: lowering the cost of living, expanding access to health care, protecting public lands, and fixing the immigration system.
priorities.quote: Congressman Vasquez has continued to win over Democrat, Republican and Independent voters because he is willing to work with anyone to deliver results for New Mexicans on the issues they care most about: lowering the cost of living, expanding access to health care, protecting our public lands, and fixing our broken immigration system.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology subcommittee) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Readiness; Strategic Forces subcommittees).

candidates.name: Greg Cunningham
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary after Jose Orozco unofficially withdrew.

summary.text: Greg Cunningham is the Republican nominee for New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District. A U.S. Marine Corps veteran and longtime Albuquerque Police Department officer and detective, he also owned a private investigations agency. He lost two campaigns for the New Mexico House before running for Congress, and his campaign website lists border security, energy development, the economy and public safety among his priorities.

background.text: Describes himself as a lifelong New Mexican; the Santa Fe New Mexican reports he grew up in Albuquerque's southwest valley.
Joined the U.S. Marine Corps, where, according to his campaign website, he served as a combat veteran and Recon Marine; in a campaign ad he says his service began in 1987.

Served with the Albuquerque Police Department, including as an undercover detective according to his campaign website; NM Political Report reports he was a police detective in Albuquerque for more than two decades.
Is a former owner of a private investigations agency, according to Ballotpedia, and describes himself on his campaign website as a business owner.
Ran for New Mexico House District 29 in 2022 and 2024, losing both times to Rep. Joy Garratt (D).
Launched his campaign for the 2nd Congressional District in October 2025; Yvette Herrell, the former congresswoman, endorsed him for the Republican nomination, and he won the June 2, 2026 primary.
According to his campaign website, he is married to Jennifer and is a father and grandfather; the Santa Fe New Mexican reports he lost his wife to cancer in 2010.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists six priorities: keep the border secure, develop American energy, protect New Mexico's way of life, build a stronger economy, invest in New Mexico's children, and make New Mexico safe.
priorities.quote: Keep the Border Secure Develop American Energy Protect Our New Mexico Way of Life Build a Stronger Economy Invest in New Mexico Children Make New Mexico Safe

positions.summary: Lists "Keep the Border Secure" as a top campaign priority.
